decisions.reason: As a 2023 flagship still featured on the home page and tightly aligned with the firm's core dosimetry and QA capabilities, it remains a high-value option with little reason to abandon now.

The oncology risk-management software is still somewhat market-uncertain and likely slower to scale than core measurement products, but its standalone presence and strategic fit with integrated QA argue for keeping the option open.
This 2024 CT image-quality phantom is very new, close to the firm's imaging QA direction, and too early in its learning cycle to justify withdrawal unless uptake proves clearly weak.

The mammography image-quality phantom serves a narrower niche and may overlap with adjacent imaging QA offerings, raising exit likelihood somewhat, but the product is still too new to drop immediately.

The full-field mammography test phantom appears similarly niche and potentially substitutable within the firm's imaging QA portfolio, so it has the highest abandonment risk though still below the threshold for dropping now.

Because this 2024 imaging QA instrument line is presented as a strategic focus and fits the firm's expansion into integrated independent QA, management would likely continue supporting it while uncertainty resolves.
